instagram_caption:
Swiping all your apps closed does not save battery.

Apple's own guide says you should only close an app if it's unresponsive. Reopening a closed app means loading it from scratch, and that startup burst uses power. When a user asked if quitting apps helps battery life, Apple software chief Craig Federighi replied "no and no" (MacRumors, 2016).

What really drains it: a bright screen, GPS, and apps that keep working in the background, like music or maps. Settings > Battery shows the real culprits.

The lesson: close an app only when it freezes.

Source: TechRadar and MacRumors, checked Nov 19, 2026.

Swiping apps closed is one of the most common phone habits, and it does not save battery. Apple's guide says to close an app only if it's unresponsive, reopening an app from scratch costs a burst of power, and Apple's software chief Craig Federighi answered "no and no" when asked if he quits apps for battery life. The real drains are screen brightness, GPS and apps that keep working in the background.
